newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore share market tumbles, led by property.
newsitem.headline: Singapore share market tumbles, led by property.

text.p: The Singapore stock market tumbled on Friday, led by property counters, dealers said.
Straits Steamship Land, DBS Land and UIC fell in active trade to new year lows. Heavyweight CityDev also fell S$0.30 to S$10.80. The SES Property Index ended 10.23 down to 631.89.

Dealers attributed the sell-off to news that a recent government land sale of office sites attracted sharply lower prices. They added that weak sentiment and a poor economic outlook also hit other counters.
"It's a terrible day. The blue-chips just got whacked," a dealer said, adding foreign investors were among the sellers.

The Straits Times Industrials Index fell below psychological support of 2,100 to end down 1.61 percent or 33.92 points, at 2,076.65. Volume was light at 66.6 million shares, with decliners leading advances 230 to 86.
Singapore Press Foreign was among the losers, shedding S$0.30 to S$23.30 on reports its advertisement revenue has declined.
Malaysian Causeway Invest continued to lead the actives, with 4.4 million shares, including 2.3 million shares crossed at S$1.50 and S$1.60.
